questions.qtext:
Consider the following graph G:

Which of the following options are correct?

options.text: The sum of the weights of an spanning free formed using Kruskal’s algorithm on G is 39.
The set of edges in the spanning of G tree using Kruskal’s algorithm are (A, D), (C, E), (D, B), (A, B), (B, E) and (G, E).
The set of edges in the spanning free of G using Kruskal’s algorithm are (A, D), (C, E), (D, F), (A, B), (B, E) and (G, E).
The sum of the weights of the spanning free formed using Kruskal’s algorithm on G is 35.

questions.solution:
(a, c)
MST of G will have AD, CE, DF, AB, BE, GE as edges. Hence, sum will be
(5 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 7 + 9) = 39

questions.qtext:
Which of the following is/are correct regarding AVL tree?
S1 : In an AVL tree, during the insert operation there are atmost two rotations required.
S2 : AVL tree can be used to implement an optimal comparison based sorting algorithm.
questions.solution:
(c)
S1 : The AVL property is restored on every operation. Therefore inserting another item will require at most two rotations to restore the balance.
S2 : AVL tree can be used to sort N numbers in Ο(N log N) time, by inserting all the numbers in the tree, and iteratively calling next largest N times.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: Prim’s minimum spanning tree algorithm can be used to most efficiently find whether a cycle is present in a given graph.
Breadth first search can be used to most efficiently find whether a cycle is present in a given graph.
Depth first search can be used to most efficiently find whether a cycle is present in a given graph.
Kruskal’s minimum spanning tree algorithm can be used to most efficiently find whether a cycle is present in a given graph.

questions.solution:
(c)
DFS is well-suited for cycle detection because it can efficiently find back edges indicating cycle,making. It the most efficient for the purpose.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: In a min-heap, the next largest element of any element can be found is Ο(log n) time.
In a BST, finding the next smallest element to given element can be done is Ο(n) time.
Binary insertion sorting requires Ο(n log n) total operations.
Any n-node unbalanced tree can be balanced using Ο(log n) rotations.

questions.solution:
(b)
(a) False: A min-heap can provide next largest element, we need to do a linear search through the heap’s array it will take Ο(n) time.
(b) True: Finding the next smallest element, the predecessor, may require traveling down the height of the tree, making the running time Ο(n).
(c) False: Binary insertion sorting improve the time it take to find right position for next element being inserted. It may still take Ο(n) time to perform swaps necessary to shift it into place.
This results is an Ο(n2) running time, the same as that of insertion sort.
(d) False: The worst case unbalanced tree is a list, and balancing it require Ο(n) rotations.
